name: Waymo
summary: Waymo operates fully autonomous ride-hailing services and develops the Waymo Driver, a self-driving system for passenger and commercial mobility.
overview: Waymo is Alphabet's autonomous-driving business, commercializing the Waymo Driver through a growing driverless ride-hailing network.

facts.label: Latest financing
facts.note: Announced February 2026 at a $126B post-money valuation.

bull_case: Waymo has a leading commercial autonomous-driving product, deep Alphabet backing, and a data advantage that can compound as it enters more cities.
bear_case: Fleet ownership, regulation, local operations, and a long path to unit economics make scaling autonomy capital intensive.
directory_notes: 400,000+ weekly rides in six U.S. metros at the time of financing
Global city expansion and fleet economics.

intelligence.description: Waymo develops the Waymo Driver and runs a fully autonomous ride-hailing service. Its core question is no longer whether driverless rides work, but whether operations can scale across cities with attractive economics.
company: Waymo began as Google’s self-driving-car project and now operates as Alphabet’s autonomous mobility business. Its Waymo One service turns the technical stack into a consumer product: a rider requests a car through an app and travels without a human driver.

The company’s February 2026 financing marked a transition from technical validation to network build-out. Waymo said it had surpassed 20 million lifetime rides, provided more than 400,000 rides per week across six major U.S. metropolitan areas, and planned to reach more than 20 additional cities during 2026.
intelligence.why_it_matters: Waymo is a rare private company attempting to build a physical-world AI platform at national scale. Its progress shapes the opportunity set for private autonomy, fleet, mapping, simulation, and automotive-supply companies, while creating a future public-market comparable for mobility platforms and Alphabet.

changed.text: Waymo raised external capital after operating for years inside Alphabet.
Closed a $5.6B investment round to support product and geographic expansion.
More than tripled annual ride volume to 15 million rides, according to the company.
Raised $16B at a $126B post-money valuation and outlined expansion to more than 20 additional cities.

takeaways: Waymo has moved from a research project into a paid mobility network with meaningful ride volume.
Alphabet remains the majority investor, giving Waymo capital and technical support few competitors can match.
The investment case depends on whether city-by-city expansion converts a safety and data lead into durable unit economics.
Regulation, fleet costs, and operational complexity remain the central constraints on the path to scale.
